cases.description: A messaging-capable position with course, speed and a comment.
A message wanting an ack: the addressee padded to 9 characters, the ID after {.
Message text over 67 characters: receivers accept it, but a sender must not write it.
Comment text that would read back as an /A= altitude: the encoder must refuse it rather than change its meaning.
PARM. names at most 13 channels (5 analog, 8 digital); a 14th is refused.
EQNS. carries three coefficients for each of the five analog channels: 15 in all.
A comment starting with / gets a / delimiter in front, since a decoder drops one leading / or space.
A comment starting with a space gets a / delimiter in front, since a decoder drops one leading / or space.
A comment that looks like course/speed gets a / delimiter in front, so it is not read as a data extension.
The encoder refuses an object name ending in a space: trailing spaces are padding and would not read back.
Every optional element of a position report at once, in the canonical order.
A position report with nothing optional.
A message carrying its own ID and a reply-ack for the other station's message.
The encoder refuses message text with {.
The encoder refuses addressee over 9 characters.
The encoder refuses ack with its own message ID.
The encoder refuses object name over 9 characters.
The encoder refuses object without timestamp.
The encoder refuses item name too short.
The encoder refuses weather report with a comment.
The encoder refuses weather without the weather symbol.
The encoder refuses two data extensions.
The encoder refuses PHG in a compressed report.
The encoder refuses ambiguity in a compressed report.
The encoder refuses latitude beyond 90.
The encoder refuses invalid symbol table.
The encoder refuses a comment that reads as altitude.
The encoder refuses a comment containing PHG text, which default decoding lifts out.
The encoder refuses a comment that reads as a DAO.
The encoder refuses a comment with a line break.
The encoder refuses status with a non-DHM timestamp.
The encoder refuses NMEA sentence whose checksum doesn't match.
The encoder refuses telemetry with 4 channels.
A voice frequency straight after a 7-byte data extension is separated from it by /.
An object carrying a weather report.
A compressed position with course and speed; coordinates round to the nearest base-91 step.
Text is sent as UTF-8: the degree sign is the two bytes C2 B0.
The spec's Mic-E worked example: latitude, the Returning message and the +100 longitude offset go into the destination, the rest into the information field.
A Mic-E grid locator goes first in the status text with /G, then a space before the comment.
A Mic-E comment that would read back as a grid locator gets a / delimiter in front.
The encoder refuses a status timestamp whose hour is 42, as it does in a position or object report; a decoder reads it with a warning.
The encoder refuses a bit-sense project title of 24 characters; the spec allows 23. A decoder accepts a longer one.
A project title of 23 characters is written, even when it is more than 23 bytes in UTF-8.
The encoder refuses a Mic-E report whose message bits mix standard and custom ones, which has no defined meaning.
A capabilities report must list at least one capability.
An NWS bulletin is addressed NWS- or NWS_; NWSBOT is not one.

An exact position sent with two digits of ambiguity: the blanked digits hide where it is within the minute, but the minute written is the one it is in (51.4543 is 51 degrees 27.258 minutes, so 27, not 26).
Rev 0 Mic-E binary telemetry with a value of 255: it would be taken for 0xFF padding and removed on the way back in, so an encoder refuses it.
A PHG height code above 9 is written as the ASCII character after 9 (: for 10), as the spec allows for balloons and aircraft.
A GGA compressed position at sea level: the cs bytes cannot hold 0 feet, so they carry the nearest (1 foot) and /A= carries the altitude, as for any altitude they cannot hold exactly.
A compressed position carries course/speed or a range in its cs bytes, not both, so an encoder refuses both.
The compressed range is 2 x 1.08^s miles; a range under 2 miles is outside the format and is refused, not moved to 2.
Mic-E status text must not start with a type code character, so a comment that does is written after a /.
A value holding a control character would read back as free text, so the encoder refuses it.
A value starting with a space would read back without it, so the encoder refuses it.
A { in NWS bulletin text would read back as brace-in-message-text, so the encoder refuses it.
A { in a bit-sense project title would read back as brace-in-message-text, so the encoder refuses it.
NWS bulletin text has no length limit (APRS12c ch. 14), so 78 characters are written.
A footprint latitude of 100.02 degrees is refused.
A control byte as the user ID is written back as it came (APRS12c ch. 19 places no restriction on user-defined data).
An Agrelo bearing of 361 degrees is refused.
A query type the spec does not define has no fixed length, so its target is written after one space.
A pressure of 986.9499999999999 mbar is within 1e-6 of a step's half, so it is the half 9869.5 tenths and is written 9870, away from zero.
A temperature of -0.5 F lies halfway between -1 and 0 and rounds away from zero, to -1.

0.9764166666666666 degrees is 58.584999999999996 minutes, the half 58.585 within the tolerance, so both the latitude and the (negative) longitude are written 58.59 minutes, rounded once from the degrees given.
An altitude of -0.5 feet rounds away from zero to -1 foot.
A gust of 999.4 mph rounds to 999, which the three-digit field holds.
A gust of 999.5 mph rounds to 1000, which the three-digit field cannot hold, so it is refused.
A humidity of 99.7 percent rounds to 100, written h00.
0.005 inches of rain is half a hundredth and rounds up to r001.
An RNG range of 24.5 miles rounds to 25.
A Mic-E speed of 0.5 knots rounds up to 1 knot.
A footprint radius of 199.5 miles rounds to 200 whole miles.
A course of 360.4 degrees rounds to 360, which is north and is written.
0.995 inches rounds to 1.00 in hundredths and 1.0 in tenths, a whole number, so it is written as three digits.
9.96 inches rounds to 10.0 in tenths, not under 10, so it is written whole.
999.5 inches rounds to 1000, which three characters cannot hold.
A !DAO! with no extra digits (!W  !) on an ambiguous position still reads back with dao-with-ambiguity, so there is no clean form.
The cs bytes hold a course and a speed together, so a course alone would add a speed the data does not have.
The cs bytes hold a course and a speed together, so a speed alone would add a course the data does not have.
h00 is 100 percent (APRS12c ch. 12), so 0 percent has no form.
A humidity of 0.4 percent rounds to 0, which has no form.
Only one data extension follows the symbol; a PHG after a course/speed could only go later in the comment, where it reads back with data-extension-in-comment.
A DF bearing extends the course/speed, so an RNG with it could only go later in the comment, where it reads back with data-extension-in-comment.
An area does not count as the data extension, so a well-formed RNG later in the comment reads back as a range: the text has no clean form.
A DF bearing with no course and speed goes after .../..., the unknown form; 000/000 would be a fixed DF station.
Storm data with no course and speed goes after .../..., the form that reads back as unknown.
A voice frequency after a DF bearing follows a /, as after a seven-byte extension.
A voice frequency after storm data follows a /, as after a seven-byte extension.
An inner packet that reads back with only an info diagnostic (a plain message whose text starts ?APRSM) is written: an info is not a defect.
Analog values given as numbers: a whole number from 0 to 999 is three digits (5, 0, 190.0), any other the shortest plain decimal (1.5, 1000).
0.53 has a 0 before its point, -5 is not padded, 91.0 is whole and three digits.
EQNS. coefficients given as numbers: no trailing .0, and 1e61 as a 1 and 61 zeros, with no exponent.
-94.0 is -94 and 1e-7 is 0.0000001, with no exponent.
A footprint latitude of 34.0 given as a number is 34, after the leading space a positive value takes.
A positive longitude gets a leading space as a positive latitude does, and the radius is four digits.
No form reads back with the first channel empty after MIC (T#MIC,,033 reads back otherwise), so there is no clean form.
A latitude that disagrees with the sentence's would read back as the sentence's.
A compressed weather report has no comment for a /A=, so a GGA altitude of 10000 feet goes in the cs bytes as the nearest step, 1.002^4610 (about 10004.5) feet.
A footprint latitude and longitude of 0 each take the leading space, as north and east do.
Without its space a latitude of 0 would join the query type (?WX?0).
A Mic-E locator followed by base-91 telemetry, with no comment: telemetry is lifted before the locator is read, so it is written straight after it.
A Mic-E locator followed by a !DAO!, with no comment, is written straight after it.
A locator is only read at the start of the status text, so comment text that looks like one after a PHG is written straight on.
Comment text that looks like a locator after an RNG is text, written straight on.
An uncompressed course of 0 is written 000, which APRS12c ch. 7 gives as unknown and reads back as 0.
A Mic-E course of 0 reads back as no course (APRS12c ch. 10: unknown or indefinite), so it is refused.
A compressed c of 0 reads back as 360, so a course of 0 is refused.
A course of -0.3 rounds to 0, written 000 in an uncompressed report.
A Mic-E course of -0.3 rounds to 0, which Mic-E cannot hold as a course, so it is refused.
A PHG straight after a Mic-E locator and its space is lifted before a later altitude is looked for, so its digits 060} are not read as one.
A compressed speed of -0.03 knots is nearest the step s = 0 and is written as 0.
A compressed speed of -0.3 knots is nearest s = -5 on the cs speed scale, outside the byte, so it is refused rather than moved to 0.
A compressed range of 1.95 miles is nearer the step 2 miles (s = 0) than 1.852 (s = -1), so it is written as 2.
A compressed range of 1.9 miles is nearest the step s = -1 (1.852 miles), outside the byte, so it is refused.
A compressed position with a range but no compression type gets the default type byte C (current fix, other source, software), as a late RNG moved into the cs bytes does.
Bulletin text of 67 characters is written: the limit counts characters (code points), and this text is 67 of them though it is 68 UTF-16 units and 71 bytes.

encode.text: ADRAD Bastel Owend al 📡Donneschden um 17h Rue du Couvent n°4,Digi

expect.info: :BLN0     :  ADRAD Bastel Owend al 📡Donneschden um 17h Rue du Couvent n°4,Digi

cases.description: A compressed course of 1.2 degrees is 1 in whole degrees, so it is known, and its nearest 4-degree step is north, written c = 0.
A compressed course of 0.3 degrees is 0 in whole degrees, an unknown course, which the cs bytes cannot hold.
A compressed course of -0.7 degrees is -1 in whole degrees, outside 1-360, so it is refused, though its nearest 4-degree step would be north.
